title: The Mango Both of Them Were Watching

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Two villagers have both been watching the same perfect mango for a week: claim it first, or split it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: For a week, (subject) has been watching one particular mango ripen on the tree behind the huts: golden, round, perfect. Today, as (subject) arrives to pick it, (subject.he/she) finds (friend) already standing under the tree, gazing up at the same mango with the same expression. It turns out (friend) has been watching it for a week too.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I've been watching it for a week," says (subject). "So have I." "I saw it first." "Did you, though?" They argue about it for some time. While they argue, a bird lands on the branch and starts eating the mango. They watch in silence. "...We could share the next one," says (friend). They spend the following week watching it together.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: They pick it together and cut it exactly in half, very carefully, measuring with a stick. It's the best mango either of them has ever eaten, and they agree it's because of all the waiting. Then each of them secretly starts watching a different mango.
